title: Analytics residency proxy and safe-write fencing
creator: Evan Cho
description:
Background:
Redwood's console ingest and analytics pipelines currently rely on region-tagged replication gates at the sink layer. This has led to two recurring operational issues: (1) transient writes from services in non-primary regions can be accepted locally and later rejected or redacted by downstream residency enforcement, resulting in partial events and broken deduplication; (2) emergency evacuation/playback scenarios are complex because there is no single proxy layer that can enforce soft-fencing rules, apply in-flight annotations, or orchestrate safe eviction when a tenant crosses region boundaries.

Goal:
Design and implement an analytics residency proxy that sits upstream of our analytics replication sinks and enforces "safe-write" fencing semantics. The proxy will: (a) validate tenant-region affinity and annotate events with immutable residency metadata, (b) apply configurable soft-eviction rules (hold, quarantine, drop with tombstone) based on policy, (c) surface deterministic rejection/acceptance decisions to clients via structured error codes, and (d) provide operator controls for staged evacuation and coordinated replay.

Non-goals:
- Replacing the durable replication transport (we will integrate with existing mirror/replicator components).
- Full legal/retention policy engine. We expect residency policies to be supplied by the Console policy service (separate work).

Proposed solution (high level):
1) Residency Proxy service (RP): a small stateless service deployed in each analytics region. RP accepts writes from Console backend and SDK ingestion gateways. It looks up tenant residency metadata (from Tenant-Service cache + fallback to policy store), then returns one of three canonical decisions: ACCEPT, QUARANTINE, or REJECT.
2) Safe-write semantics: ACCEPT -> forward with residency header and sequence token. QUARANTINE -> write to a tenant-isolated quarantine stream (short TTL, flagged) and forward a tombstone/marker to the primary stream. REJECT -> return a structured 409 with reason code and suggested remediation (e.g., pin tenant, request region move).
3) Evacuation mode: RP can be flipped into evacuation orchestration where writes are automatically diverted to a target-region mirror while emitting audit markers for replay. A one-click operator flow in Console will coordinate switching the proxy's target map, draining KV caches and gating consumption.
4) Observability & tracing: every decision logged with decision_id and trace_id; metrics exported for acceptance rate, quarantine volume, rejection rate, and average decision latency.
5) Backwards compatibility: when RP is disabled, behavior falls back to existing sink acceptance (default accept).

Implementation phases:
- Phase 1 (MVP, 2 sprints): service skeleton, tenant metadata cache, basic decision logic (accept/quarantine/reject), integration tests with mirror writer and Console ingestion, structured decision codes.
- Phase 2 (policy integration, 2 sprints): plug into Console policy store, add soft-eviction configurable actions, metrics dashboards and alerting.
- Phase 3 (evacuation & operator flows, 2-3 sprints): evacuation orchestration, safe drain, replay helpers, UI hooks.

Success metrics:
- Decision latency p95 < 12ms for cache-hit path.
- Quarantine write throughput scales to 10k rps per region in MVP configuration.
- Reduction in downstream partial/invalid events by 95% in tenants covered by RP after rollout.
- Operators can complete a tenant evacuation (switch+drain) within SLA (target < 30 minutes for sample tenant class).

Risks and mitigation:
- Policy divergence between RP and policy store -> mitigate with nightly reconciliation job and strict schema validation.
- Increased ingest latency -> conservative default: keep RP in pass-through accept mode for performance-sensitive tenants and roll out gradually.
- Quarantine storage growth -> implement TTL and automatic compaction, add quota per-tenant.

Open questions:
- What is the source-of-truth for residency during emergency (policy store vs manual override)?
- Should QUARANTINE be writable to customer-accessible logs or only operator-only stores?
- How to represent multi-tenant writes that span regions (batched ingestion from cross-region aggregator)?
